title: What a content pack should be allowed to change about the world
question: Taking RimWorld and The Sims as the standard the owner has set, what kinds of change does a modder of a life-and-politics game actually reach for first, and what is the smallest set of declarable effects that would cover most of them without letting a pack write arbitrary code?
whyItMatters: The pack loader ships and works, but a pack may declare only scenes and activity durations: there is no effects field, no effect kind vocabulary and no apply step anywhere in the codebase. So a modder can add a conversation and cannot change a single thing about the world through it, which is the whole distance between what ships and the modding standard the owner named as governing every system.
usableAnswer: A ranked list of effect kinds a pack should be able to declare, each with what it reads, what it writes and a worked example of a mod somebody would actually publish. Plus the line the researcher would draw between an effect the loader validates and applies itself and a change that has to stay in the game's own code, with the reason for the line.

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Defines the whole pack surface: the ordinary-scenes-v1 api, a 128 KiB ceiling, authored-fiction authority, and exactly three declarable keys — dependencies, durations and scenes. It establishes the limit and offers no view on what should be added.

sourcesChecked.source: examples/content-packs/, the two shipped example packs
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Shows a working encounter and a timing pack. Neither changes world state, because nothing in the format can.

sourcesChecked.source: A repository-wide search for an effect vocabulary — effectKind, EffectKind, applyEffect
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Returns nothing. The three types named Effect in the tree are read-only projections of consequences that already happened, not a vocabulary a pack could declare into.

sourcesChecked.source: src/simulation/production-catalog.ts lines 146-190, the production catalogue boundary
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Shows that a new world ships with empty policy, metric, causal-mechanism, incident and mortality catalogues and throws if unestablished content is added. It constrains where pack content could land without saying what a pack should carry.

notes: The owner's standard is explicit and is not negotiable here: content is data, discovered rather than imported, modder-friendly in the way RimWorld and The Sims are. The question is what that means concretely for this game, not whether to do it.

An effect a pack declares has to leave the same kind of record a first-party action leaves, because the history store is what the save and every later reading are built on. An effect that writes nothing readable is not worth admitting.
No proprietary material from those games. What is wanted is the shape of what modders reach for, not their content.
